transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I came in because... it's just getting really hard at work. I make jewelry, mostly custom pieces and repairs, and lately, when people ask me a simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready, my answer just starts going all over the place. I'll start talking about their invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about the garden soil I bought over the weekend, and then the mortgage papers... which reminds me, the bank sent me this letter that was so confusing, it had all these extra forms. I used to be so good with paperwork when I was taking some college classes, but now it's just a mess. Anyway, I can see the customers just losing me, just staring at me like they have no idea what I'm saying.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood being unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with having a lot more energy than usual?

No, I haven't really felt high or energetic like that. Honestly, it's been the opposite, just feeling kind of heavy. But speaking of energy, I did try this new herbal tea that my neighbor gave me. She said it was supposed to boost your metabolism or something. She's always bringing over these little care packages because she knows I work from home a lot. She has this beautiful golden retriever that just barks at the mailman every single day at exactly 10:30. It's almost like clockwork. I don't know how the mailman stands it, really. He always wears those shorts, even when it's freezing out. But no, I haven't had any extra energy or felt really happy or irritable lately.
You mentioned feeling 'heavy' lately—have you been feeling sad, down, or low in mood most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Yeah, I have. Most mornings I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness... it's like the color has just drained out of the house before I even get to the shop. My shop is attached to the garage, which used to be so convenient. We converted it back in... oh, it must have been 2015? Or 2016. My husband did most of the drywall himself, which was a huge mess. Dust everywhere for weeks. You could write your name in the dust on the kitchen counter. I tried using that special vacuum attachment, the one with the little bristles, but it didn't really help. I ended up just wiping everything down with wet rags. But yeah, that heavy feeling is just there, almost every day.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others have told you aren't true or don't make sense to them?

Well, sometimes... yeah, actually. When the shop is really quiet, I'll hear a woman's voice just kind of muttering my name. It usually sounds like it's coming from the polishing room. And sometimes I'll smell burning metal, even when all the torches are completely off. It feels so real that I actually get up and go check. Which is a hassle because my polishing room is all the way in the back, past the safe. I bought that safe second-hand from a guy who used to run a pawn shop downtown. He was retiring and moving to Florida... Naples, I think. Or maybe Sarasota. He told me all about how the humidity there is terrible for certain metals, which is true, you really have to watch out for tarnish if you're keeping silver down there. I always tell my customers to keep those little silica gel packets in their jewelry boxes. You know, the ones that say 'do not eat' on them? My sister's kid actually tried to eat one once, it was a whole ordeal at the hospital... but anyway, yeah, I hear the voice and smell the metal, and I always go check, but there's never anyone there.
Do these experiences of hearing your name and smelling burning metal happen only during the times you're feeling that heavy, low mood, or do they also occur even when your mood feels more normal?

Well, no, it's not just when I'm feeling down. There was actually a stretch before this heavy feeling really settled in... I was feeling fine, honestly. I was still running my jewelry making classes and spending a lot of time out gardening. My hydrangeas were absolutely spectacular this year. I finally got the soil acidity right so they turned that beautiful deep blue. You have to use aluminum sulfate for that, otherwise they just stay this washed-out pink color. Working with metals, you learn a lot about how chemicals react, so I just applied that to the garden. My neighbor—the one with the golden retriever—she asked what my secret was, and I told her it's all about the soil pH. She tried it but I think she used too much and burned the roots. It's a delicate balance, you really can't rush it. You have to test the soil first with those little strips. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the shop. Even during that good stretch, for several weeks I kept hearing those noises from the polishing room. And I was also getting really worried that my customers were watching the business. Like, just keeping an eye on the place for some reason. So yeah, it happens even when my mood is totally normal.

Thinking back over the entire time you've had these experiences—hearing your name and smelling burning metal—how many weeks or months in total have you had them, and how does that compare to how long you've been feeling this heavy, depressed mood?

Well, if I look at the whole picture... the heavy, bleak mood has really been there for most of the time this has all been going on. It's not just a bad week here or there. It's the sadness, and I haven't been sleeping well at all, and I hardly have an appetite... plus this awful guilt I keep feeling. It's just part of my daily life now. Which is really hard when you're trying to run a business. 

I used to love making breakfast before heading out to the shop. I had this great recipe for blueberry scones. I'd use fresh blueberries when they were in season, usually around July. There's a farm about forty minutes from here where you can go pick them yourself. My husband and I used to go every summer. He'd always eat half of what he picked before we even got to the weighing scale. The lady who runs the place—Mrs. Higgins, I think her name is—she always pretended not to notice, but I know she did. She had these beautiful antique scales, the kind with the cast iron base and the brass weights. I always admired the patina on that brass. You can't fake a good patina, it takes years of oils from people's hands and exposure to the air. I tried explaining that to a customer once who wanted me to artificially age a silver locket, using liver of sulfur. It works, sure, but it just doesn't look the same as true, natural aging. Liver of sulfur smells terrible, too, like rotten eggs... 

But anyway, what I mean is, the mood and the sleep problems and everything else, they've been dragging on for the vast majority of the time I've been dealing with the noises and the smells. It's just been a constant weight.
